title: Sustainable Inference Efficiency — experiment ledger and rollout plan
creator: Maya Patel
description:
Summary:
This initiative centralizes a prioritized experiment ledger and staged rollout plan to reduce per-token inference cost while maintaining p95 latency and QA thresholds. Scope covers: adaptive batching heuristics, prefix/KV cache eviction policies and TTLs, and two quantization profiles (8-bit and mixed-precision quant). The ledger ties experiments to measurable OKRs (cost per 1M tokens, p95 latency, error/regression rate on eval sets) and maps learnings to rollout gates for Hosted API and Dedicated pools.

Goals (90-day):
- Reduce median cost-per-response by 18% for conversational workloads and 12% for embeddings workloads.
- Preserve p95 latency within +10% of baseline for high-priority routes.
- Keep model-output quality regressions under 1.5% (measured via held-out prompt sets and automated evals).

Key deliverables:
- Canonical experiment ledger (this ticket): prioritized experiments, owners, acceptance criteria, and rollback plan.
- Dashboards: cost delta by customer-tier & route, token-econ heatmap, regressions alert.
- Two staged rollouts: canary -> cohort -> global with automatic rollback rules.

Acceptance criteria for each experiment:
- Clear hypothesis and metric (A/B or pre/post).
- Observability: per-route cost and quality traces hooked to console dashboards.
- Defined rollback condition and SLO impact analysis.

Constraints & trade-offs:
- Aggressive quantization could reduce cost but increase hallucination/quality drift on long-form generation. We will gate quant experiments behind model-level eval suites and small-scale customer beta.
- Larger batching windows reduce per-token compute but can increase tail latency; experiments must include latency budget simulations and synthetic peak tests.

Stakeholders:
- PM lead: Maya Patel (creator)
- Eng leads: Lin Chen (runtime), Javier Morales (serving infra)
- Research: Dr. Priya Nair (quantization)
- DX/Design: Ava Thompson (console flows)
- SRE/Observability: Noor Aziz

Artifacts & links:
- Experiment ledger (working doc): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Sustainable+Inference+Experiment+Ledger
- Experiment design template: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1qXx-example
- GitHub experiment harness PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/4987
- Cost dashboard prototype: https://dash.redwood.ai/d/cost/proto-sustainable-inference

Rollout plan (high level):
- Milestone 1 (by 2026-03-31): finalize ledger and instrument primary metrics; run smoke tests for batching heuristics on test fleets.
- Milestone 2 (by 2026-04-30): complete two KV-cache policy field trials and one quantization micro-benchmark; internal review and signoff.
- Milestone 3 (by 2026-05-31): canary rollouts for conservative batching + cache policy on 5% of traffic; continuous monitoring and quality audits.
- Milestone 4 (by 2026-06-30): staged expansion to Dedicated clusters and public rollout if acceptance criteria met.

Risks & mitigation:
- Risk: Quality regressions not caught by automated evals. Mitigation: partner with Research for expanded evaluation suites and invite early-access customers for human review.
- Risk: Observability gaps lead to blind rollouts. Mitigation: instrument per-route token accounting and push alerts for deviations beyond thresholds.

Longer term options:
- Explore hybrid quant profiles per-model shard.
- Routing by cost-sensitivity: route low-importance traffic to quantized/fallthrough models.

Note: this ledger explicitly avoids blanket application of aggressive knobs; every global policy change must pass an experiment gating checklist.

notes:
Decision log: prefer incremental rollouts with canary cohorts rather than config-wide flips. We will codify rollback rules in the runbook.
Follow-ups: set bi-weekly syncs with SRE for alert thresholds; schedule a demo for execs post-Milestone 2.
